_comment: Scenes (docs/ADVENTURES.md §5.18, §8.11; game/story/stage.py): choreography played on a town's map by its own people. cues: the whitelist in stage.CUES (pick, arrive, walk, run, follow, flee, say, shout, give, take, kneel, rise, fall, die, crowd, disperse, door, bell, focus, wait, hold, release, talk, beat, fight, read), each with its own keys (who, role, to, at, words or key, letter, ticks, always...). words: lines for a cue's key. A pick that finds nobody sends the scene to its end, where only cues marked always still play.

runner.about: A child or a serving hand runs up to you through the street and presses a sealed letter into your hand from people who need you; its page opens, then the tale's hook.

call: You - the one with the sword!
breath: They said you'd come in by this gate.
I ran the whole way. Sorry.
I saw you from the end of the street.
Nobody else would come and find you.
plea: They said give it to you and nobody else.
It's from the elders. Read it, please.
I'm to wait while you read it.
letter:
To whoever carries a sword through {town},

{hook}

We are not fighters. We have tried, and we have buried those who tried.

What we can pay is yours. Only come.

Forgive the hand, it shakes.

{hook}

The child who brings this knows nothing of it; do not frighten them.

If you are what they say you are, you will come.

Stranger,

I write because I am too proud to beg aloud.

{hook}

There is coin set by. There is a bed. There is our thanks, for what it is worth.

To the one who came in today,

{hook}

The lord will not come. The watch will not go up there. You are what is left to us.

Burn this when you have read it.

Friend, if you will be one,

{hook}

Ask anyone in {town} and they will tell you the same, if they dare.

We will be waiting.

plea.about: Folk gather round you in the street, murmuring, and the eldest of them steps out to speak for them; the tale's hook opens.

murmur: Look at the gear on them.
Will they help, do you think?
Hush, here comes the old one.
open: Forgive us, stranger. We have no one else to ask.
You'll have heard there's trouble. Hear us out.
Don't go yet. We've a thing to ask of you.
We are plain folk, and we are frightened.
Stay a moment. This concerns us all.
